 JUDGMENT This petition is filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of .1,00,000/- along with interest from the date of petition till its realization for injuries sustained by the petitioner.

2. The case of the petitioner in brief is that on 26.07.2021 at about 10.45 a.m., when she was riding her Scooty Pep bike bearing Regn.No.KA-05-HM-1633 along with her mother Smt.Geeta.O.Patil as a pillion rider near Vidyapeeta Circle, at that time the driver of KIA Car bearing Regn.No.KA-19-ML-0973 driven by its driver at high speed in a rash and negligent manner and hit against her vehicle.

Due to which, she fell down and sustained grievous injuries and thereafter she was shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma & Orthopaedics, Byrasandra, Jayanagar,
Bengaluru, wherein she took treatment as an inpatient and spent Rs.5,000/- towards medicine,
transportation and other incidental charges.

entities.text: Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma & Orthopaedics, Byrasandra
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Prior to the accident, she was hale and healthy and she was working as Steno-typist and also taking orders for typing book work and earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, she has suffered permanent disability.
The accident occurred only due to rash and negligent driving of Car by its driver.
The respondents being driver, owner and insurer of the offending vehicle are liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
3. On service of notice, respondent No.1 did not appear before the tribunal, hence he has been placed as exparte.
The respondent No.2 & 3 have appeared before the tribunal through their respective counsel and filed their separate Written Statement.

Smt.Sheetal Venkatesh vs Sri.Manjunath.S.R on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128214774/
2
In the written statement, the respondent No.2 has denied the contents of claim petition specifically and categorically.
He also denied age, occupation and income of injured.
He has also denied the place, time and manner of accident.
The petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed.
Further contended that the driver of car was not driving the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner.

Further contended that he is the owner of above said vehicle and which was insured with respondent No.3 with a policy No.KIA/SK054326 valid from 04.08.2020 to 03.08.2023 with Engine No.G4FLLV 042553 and Chassis No.MZBEU812 TLN 122158 and further the driver of said vehicle having valid and effective driving license at the time of accident.
The amount claimed by the petitioners is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prayed for dismissal of petition.
4. The 3rd respondent in his written statement has contended that having insured the Kia car as per the policy of insurance and the liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of policy.
Further contended that the driver of car drove the same without having a valid and effective driving license.
Further the car was not at all involved in the alleged accident and same has been falsely implicated by petitioner.

Further the unfortunate accident has occurred only on account of rash and negligent riding of motor cycle by petitioner herself and due to over speed, she has lost the control over the motor cycle and fell on the road and therefore the petitioner herself, solely responsible for this unfortunate accident.
The amount claimed by the petitioners is highly exorbitant.

Hence,
prayed for dismissal of petition.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following:
ISSUES 1. Whether petitioner proves that, she sustained grievous injuries in the accident that occurred on 26.07.2021 at about 10.45 a.m., near Vidyapeeta Kattriguppe Main Road,
BSK 3 rd Stage, Bengaluru City, when she was riding a Scooty Pep bearing registration No.KA-05-HM-1633 along with her mother as a pillion rider, due to the rash and negligent driving of KIA Car bearing registration No.KA-19-ML-0973 by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the claim petition?

If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom?
3.
What order or award?

6. In order to prove her case, the petitioner examined herself as PW.1 and pillion rider i.e., mother of petitioner examined as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.8 and closed her side of evidence.
The respondents did not adduce their evidence either oral or documentary.
7. I have heard the arguments from both sides and perused the material available on record.

8. Findings of this tribunal on the above issues are as under:-
Smt.Sheetal Venkatesh vs Sri.Manjunath.S.R on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128214774/
3  Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative;
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative;
 Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following:-
 -:REASONS:-
9. Issue No.1:- The petitioner has contended that on 26.07.2021 at about 10.45 a.m., Near Vidyapeeta Circle, Vidyapeeta Kattriguppe Main Road, BSK 3rd Stage, Bengaluru City, she met with an accident due to rash and negligent driving of KIA Car bearing Regn.No.KA-19-ML-0973 by its driver and she sustained grievous injuries.
10. In order to prove rash and negligent driving of KIA Car bearing Regn.No.KA-19-ML-0973 by its driver, the petitioner examined herself as PW.1.
In her chief examination she has deposed that due to rash and negligent driving of car by its driver the accident occurred.
The petitioner also examined pillion rider by name Smt. Geeta as PW2.
In her chief examination she has deposed that due to rash and negligent driving of car by its driver the accident occurred.
On perusal of cross-examination of PW.1 and 2 nothing has been elicited from the mouth of PW.1 and 2 to disprove the case of petitioner.
11. Further, in order to prove accident, the petitioner has produced Ex.P.1 FIR lodged by Kumari.Sawan.B.V., D/o.Venkatesh.B.S on 26.07.2021.
Ex.P.2 IMV Report, wherein mentioned the damages caused to vehicle.
Ex.P.8 - Wound certificate, it shows that petitioner has sustained injuries in the road traffic accident.

After completion of investigation, the police have filed charge sheet as per Ex.P.3 against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.279, 337 and Sec.134(a&b) of IPC and R/w.Sec.187 of M.V.Act.
The petitioner has produced Ex.P.4 Order sheet of C.C.No.4082/2021, the accused appeared before the Metrapolitan Magistrate Traffic Court - IV, Bengaluru pleaded guilty and paid fine of Rs.5,000/-.

entities.text: Metrapolitan Magistrate Traffic Court - IV, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: On meticulous perusal of entire case the respondents did not place any material to disprove the case of petitioner.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 and 2 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P4 & 8, this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of KIA Car bearing Regn.No.KA-19-ML-0973 by its driver and petitioner sustained injuries.
Hence, I answered Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:
In view of held issue No.1 in the Affirmative, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

To assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several factors like injury,
pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment and medical attendants, conveyance.
13.

The petitioner contended that due to accident she sustained sutured CLW 4cm x 1cm on the right arm, swelling and other injuries on right leg and later discharged with an advice to take follow up treatment.

In order to prove the injuries caused to her, she has produced wound certificate issued by Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma & Orthopaedics marked at Ex.P.8, wherein doctor has opined that injuries are simple in nature.

entities.text: Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma & Orthopaedics
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: In order to prove disability, the petitioner has not produced any disability certificate or not examined the doctor to show that she has permanent disability.

The Smt.Sheetal Venkatesh vs Sri.Manjunath.S.R on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128214774/
4
petitioner has not produced any medical bills.
The petitioner has not examined the doctor to prove her disability.
So, in the absence of proper evidence, this tribunal cannot award compensation under the head of future loss of income and other heads.

By considering the facts and circumstances of the case and also the injuries sustained by the petitioner, the petitioner is entitled for Global compensation of .30,000/-.
14.

In MFA.No.100090 of 2014 C/w. MFA.No.25107 of 2013 between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs. Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka at Page No.7 at Para No.15 held as follows:
"However, the provisions of Section 149(1) of the Act to the extent they speak of interest payable on the compensation amount is in the nature of an exception to the general law enacted in 169 of the M.V.Act and therefore, the provisions of Section 34 of CPC to that extent become invocable on the general principles of construction of statutes namely the special law overrides the general law.

entities.text: Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs. Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, in the absence of any other law relating to interest on Judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Section 34 of CPC, 1908.

Thus, in the given circumstances of this case,
interest at the rate of more than 6% could not have been awarded."

In view of ratio and dictum laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the above judgment, the petitioner is entitled for interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
15. The petitioner has filed petition against the respondents No.1 to 3.
It is already held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of KIA Car bearing Regn.No.KA-19-ML-0973 by its driver.
The police authorities have not filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.181 of M.V.Act.
So, the respondent No.2 and 3 being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, Issue No.2 answered Partly in the Affirmative.
16. Issue No.3:

In view of the findings given on the above said issues, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioner Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for Global  compensation amount of .30,000/-
 (Rupees Thirty Thousand only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.
Respondent No.2 and 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to petitioner.
Respondent No.3 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.

Smt.Sheetal Venkatesh vs Sri.Manjunath.S.R on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128214774/
5
Entire compensation amount shall be released in favour of petitioner as amount is meager one.

After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA No.2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated 19.8.2019.

The petitioner hereby directed to produce particulars of her Bank Account, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contained compulsorily photographs of petitioner, which is duly attested by concerned Bank.
In case of deposit of awarded amount with interest thereon by respondent, the petitioner is entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal.
The Advocate fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw up award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer over computer, corrected and pronounced by me in open court on this 16th day of February, 2023.)
(D.RAGHAVENDRA)
